draft.title: Chronic disease in Australia
card: Chronic diseases are health conditions that last a long time and usually develop slowly. Cardiovascular disease (diseases of the heart and blood vessels), cancers and type 2 diabetes are major examples in Australia.
These diseases share risk factors, which are things that raise the chance of getting a disease. Common ones are smoking, poor diet and physical inactivity.
Because the risk factors overlap, one change can lower the risk of several diseases. For example, regular activity helps protect against heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
Many cases can be prevented or delayed by reducing these risk factors. This is why chronic disease is a health priority.
draft.remember: Shared risk factors mean one healthy change can lower the risk of several chronic diseases.

a.q: Why can a program that reduces smoking help lower the burden of several chronic diseases?
opts: Smoking is a risk factor shared by several of them
Smoking is the only cause of each of these diseases
Smoking is a symptom that appears once a disease starts
Smoking only affects diseases that start in childhood
a.why: Smoking is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and several cancers, so reducing it lowers risk across more than one disease. It is not the only cause of any of them, because other risk factors also play a part.
a.clue: Think about what the diseases have in common.

b.q: Sam is 45 and works at a desk in Bathurst. He eats mostly takeaway and rarely exercises. Which advice best matches how chronic disease can be reduced?
opts: Eat better and be more active to lower several risks
Wait for symptoms, as chronic disease cannot be prevented
Focus only on diet, as activity does not affect disease
Treat heart disease only, as other diseases are unrelated
b.why: Poor diet and inactivity are shared risk factors, so changing them can lower the chance of cardiovascular disease, some cancers and type 2 diabetes. Waiting for symptoms is wrong because many cases can be prevented or delayed.
b.clue: Which advice targets risk factors that several diseases share?

a.best: Smoking is a risk factor shared by several of them

b.best: Eat better and be more active to lower several risks

problems.detail: All three wrong options contain absolutes ('only', 'only', 'cannot'), while the right option is the only reasonable-sounding one. A student could pick it by spotting the extreme wording without knowing the idea.

a.q: Why can a program that reduces smoking help lower the burden of several chronic diseases?
opts: Smoking is a risk factor shared by several of them
Smoking is a symptom that appears once a disease starts
Smoking causes heart disease, which then causes the others
Smoking is a chronic disease that spreads to other organs
a.why: Smoking is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and several cancers, so reducing it lowers risk across more than one disease. It is not a symptom: it raises the chance of disease before any disease starts.
a.clue: Think about what the diseases have in common.

b.q: Sam is 45 and works at a desk in Bathurst. He does not smoke, eats mostly takeaway and rarely exercises. Which advice best fits how chronic disease can be reduced?
opts: Eat better and be more active to lower several risks
Stop smoking, as smoking is the shared risk factor
Wait until symptoms appear, then change his habits
Rest more, as chronic diseases tend to come on quickly
b.why: Poor diet and inactivity are Sam's risk factors, and they are shared, so changing them can lower his chance of cardiovascular disease, some cancers and type 2 diabetes. Smoking is a shared risk factor too, but Sam does not smoke, so that advice does not target his risks.
b.clue: Look at which risk factors Sam actually has.
